analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: LM2 Torah 107 is a two-sentence practical statement. The Rebbe contrasts אֲכִילָה (eating), which adds כֹּחַ וְחִיּוּת (strength and vitality) to a person, with תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף (the desire for sexual immorality), which damages and exhausts a person's vitality. He concludes that this desire is entirely unnecessary except for קִיּוּם הַמִּין (continuation of the species). None of these concepts are stated as bechina equivalences — the Rebbe is making a practical comparison, not an ontological equation. The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in the source text. Therefore, no additions to any package can be grounded in bechina language from this Torah, and no package-gap entries are warranted.
analysis_notes.reason_no_additions: The source text contains zero bechina declarations. There are no instances of 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' or equivalent equating language. The concepts mentioned (eating, vitality, sexual desire, species continuation) are discussed in causal or contrastive terms only, not as parallel aspects of the same essential nature.
